headline: Australia builds space infrastructure. SpaceX eyes wireless. Rocket Lab wins big.
deck: This week saw strategic moves in space infrastructure and defense contracts.

stories.head: Rocket Lab scores $90M Space Force contract
stories.body: Rocket Lab secured a $90 million contract from the U.S. Space Force for GEO satellite production, marking a significant win in the defense sector. This comes as the company prepares to sell $3 billion in stock, clearly showing that launching satellites is just one part of their strategy. The contract reinforces the trend of defense contracts becoming increasingly lucrative for smaller aerospace firms.
stories.soWhat: If defense contracts are the new gold rush, Rocket Lab just struck it rich while others are still panning for pennies.

stories.head: Australia's DARC site aims for 2027 readiness
stories.body: Australia's DARC site is now tracking for AUKUS partners, with full operational capability expected by 2027. This initiative is part of a broader strategy to enhance dual-use space infrastructure for strategic resilience. It’s a refreshing change to see international cooperation in space that doesn’t involve a rocket launch.
stories.soWhat: If this goes as planned, Australia might just become the new go-to partner for space collaboration—no launch required.

stories.head: SpaceX positions Starlink Mobile for urban market
stories.body: SpaceX's recent IPO filing has positioned Starlink Mobile as a serious competitor in the urban wireless market, hinting at a valuation that could shake up the crowded telecom landscape. With the secondary market valuation of SpaceX hitting $470 billion, the stakes are high for this satellite-based service. It suggests that even in a saturated market, there’s still room for disruption.
stories.soWhat: If Starlink can pull this off, it could redefine urban connectivity—just don’t expect to see any towers.

watchlist.title: Watch for Rocket Lab stock performance
watchlist.body: With the recent contract win and stock sale, Rocket Lab's market performance will be worth monitoring as investors react.

watchlist.title: AUKUS partners' next moves
watchlist.body: The operational readiness of Australia's DARC site could set the stage for more collaborative defense projects among AUKUS partners.

watchlist.title: Starlink Mobile's market entry
watchlist.body: Keep an eye on how Starlink Mobile positions itself against traditional telecom providers—this could shift market dynamics.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's growth trajectory
watchlist.body: After raising $190M, True Anomaly's developments in co-orbital security will be a key area to watch in the coming weeks.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
